subject: Log eviction policy — simulated fallout and escalation playbook
messages:
From: Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@healthsync.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@healthsync.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 08:14:02 -0700
Subject: Missing logs from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02 — urgent

Hi Markus,

We ran a reconciliation this morning and discovered that operational logs for our production namespace (healthsync-prod) between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-02 are missing from the Redlog archive. The gaps show up in our audit timeline and impact two open incidents.

Attached is a small snippet (healthsync_missing_logs_snippet.txt) showing the index range and the missing shard identifiers. Can you confirm whether a planned purge or retention-change was applied across our subprocessor bucket during that window? We need an explanation for potential DPA/data retention implications and whether any backups exist to restore these entries.

Please escalate if this is not a simple retrieval. Our compliance team is copied.

Thanks,
Audrey Lin
Head of Platform Reliability
HealthSync Inc

Attachments: healthsync_missing_logs_snippet.txt
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@healthsync.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:05:43 -07:00
Subject: Re: Missing logs from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02 — urgent

Hi Audrey — thank you for the heads-up and the snippet.

Short answer: we are treating this as high priority. Initial triage suggests it may be related to a retention index reconfiguration we rolled out during our simulated purge tests last week. I've looped in Neha (infra) and Laura (ops/legal escalation) to confirm the scope and whether backups can be restored.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Neha to confirm whether the purge test hit healthsync-prod buckets and whether the lifecycle rule was scoped correctly.
- Collect audit evidence (retention-change-audit.csv) and share a timeline.
- If data was removed inadvertently, we will evaluate a canary restore and provide a remediation timeline within 4 business hours.

We'll set up a call ASAP; what window works for you this morning?

— Markus Klein
Head of Platform Reliability Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention-change-audit.csv
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 11:30:19 -07:00
Subject: Re: Missing logs — retention index / subprocessor timeline

Markus / Laura — initial findings from the infra side below.

What happened (short):
- On 2026-10-03 at 02:05 UTC we executed a simulated purge exercise (internal tag: PURGE-SIM-2026-10) against a subset of older log shards to validate our eviction throttling. The purge job was meant to be read-only for canary namespaces but an upstream selector mis-evaluated a predicate and included healthsync-prod in the target set.
- The subprocessor (s3-backups-us-east-1) applied a lifecycle expiration to 7 snapshot objects. Those objects contained consolidated log indices for the 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02 range; they were impacted by garbage collection on 2026-10-03 02:18 UTC.

Immediate mitigation completed:
1) Terminated the purge run and disabled PURGE-SIM feature flag at 11:05 UTC.
2) Isolated the subprocessor bucket and suspended lifecycle transitions for healthsync-prod.
3) Created a forensic export (retention-change-audit.csv) with job ids and selector traces.

Restoration & rollback plan (short):
- Checkpointing: verify if cold snapshots exist in our replicated Glacier-equivalent escrow (replicated-escrows). If present, initiate a targeted restoration (ETA initial checks: 1.5 hours).
- If cold snapshots unavailable, run an index reconstruction using partial KV fragments (complex; ETA 48–72 hours).
- To limit blast radius while we restore, enable a temporary retention override for affected namespaces and disable further purge jobs.

Action owners:
- Neha: lead restore verification + runbook (rollback-runbook-v1.2.pdf attached).
- Rishi: coordinate legal evidence and DPA notification (if required).
- Markus: customer comms & SLA mitigation.

I will post progress updates to the incident channel and attach the runbook.

-Neha
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback-runbook-v1.2.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 13:00:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Missing logs — customer notification & DPA implications

Team — thanks for the quick triage. A few legal/compliance points to cover before we commit to a public statement to HealthSync: 

1) DPA / contractual obligations: we need to confirm whether the removed shards included any customer-controlled audit logs that are considered exportable under section 4.2 of the DPA (Data Retention & Forensics). If yes, we may trigger a formal incident notice under the DPA timeline (72 hours for material data loss).
2) Subprocessor notification: per schedule, we must notify HealthSync of any subprocessor action affecting retention. Rishi, please prepare the notification draft and cite the exact subprocessor (s3-backups-us-east-1) and the lifecycle policy identifier.
3) SLA remediation: we should consider an interim credit or service extension if the restoration will exceed our SLA window. Markus, please propose the customer-facing timeline so Sales/CS can align.

Customer comms draft (suggested first-line):
"We discovered a retention exercise that incorrectly included your production namespace and impacted a limited set of archived indices. We are performing targeted restoration and will provide a detailed timeline and forensic package within 24 hours."

Also, please collect the following evidence artifacts to include in the package: retention-change-audit.csv, job trace IDs, replication manifest, and the snapshot deletion timestamps. Put those into the Drive folder and share link to HealthSync compliance.

I will standby to engage Legal if we need to prepare a DPA amendment or formal notice.

-Laura
VP Operations & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Audrey Lin <audrey.lin@healthsync.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 16:02:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Missing logs from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02 — action & timeline

Audrey — quick update and plan of record.

Summary: A simulated purge test inadvertently targeted a subset of archived indices that included healthsync-prod. We have suspended the purge process, isolated the subprocessor bucket, and started restoration verification.

Planned timeline:
- 16:30 PST: initial check of replicated escrow for cold snapshots (Neha).
- 18:30 PST: confirm whether targeted restoration can start (if snapshots available) and provide an ETA for first shard restore.
- 24 hours: full forensic package uploaded to shared drive with job traces and audit CSV.

Mitigation & customer options:
- If we can restore from cold snapshots: expected partial restoration within 6–12 hours and full within 24–48 hours.
- If we must reconstruct indexes: estimated 48–72 hours and we will offer a service credit per the DPA & SLA annex.

We will schedule a brief call in 30 minutes to walk through evidence and next steps. Rishi will handle the formal notification per the DPA; Laura will confirm escalation and any need for a DPA clause invocation.

Again, apologies for the disruption. We understand the sensitivity and are treating this with full priority. I will update the shared Drive folder as artifacts are collected: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example-retention-incident

— Markus Klein
Head of Platform Reliability Ops
Redwood Inference
